vuln_id: OSS-Fuzz issue 42530184 / PcapPlusPlus GRE PPP-PPTP short header

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, so the line anchors below are grounded in this tree. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `b9ee9d613be2e30698f3c47c61184bde547c5fd5`, but the prepared ARVO workspace used the commit above.

classification.classification_note: The immediate sanitizer symptom is a 2-byte heap write in `pcpp::PPP_PPTPLayer::computeCalculateFields()`, but the source-level defect is missing length validation before `GreLayer::parseNextLayer()` treats a 3-byte GRE payload as a 4-byte `ppp_pptp_header`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42530184 (PcapPlusPlus): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 2 found by fuzz target FuzzTarget [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42530184
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source / static decode of the staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the crash against the staged PcapPlusPlus checkout at `0c95dfb3557644acc6a10060e48cfae1a61fc2f0`, so the line anchors below refer to that tree even though sample metadata names `b9ee9d613be2e30698f3c47c61184bde547c5fd5` as the vulnerable commit. The exact staged witness is `gt_results/arvo_42530184/poc` (71 bytes, sha256 `6c6d89edf944e9e513c5d5780b23d25c5cd591e01f6726e2b48a963f55a63c4a`). That file ends with exactly 31 trailing packet-data bytes `45 20 20 20 20 20 00 00 20 2f 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 88 0b 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`, and the saved ASan allocation frame proves that `PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()` materialized a 31-byte raw-packet buffer before the crash; the trace therefore grounds the packet extent in the saved run rather than in a reconstructed interpretation of the malformed savefile header. Static decoding of those 31 bytes shows an IPv4 header with `IHL == 20` and protocol byte `0x2f` (GRE). The GRE bytes at offsets 20..27 are `20 20 88 0b 20 20 20 20`: the first flags byte `0x20` sets `keyBit`, so `GreLayer::getHeaderLen()` returns 8, and the GRE protocol field `0x880b` selects PPP. That leaves only the three tail bytes `20 20 20` as the would-be PPP payload. Vulnerable `GreLayer::parseNextLayer()` still executes `new PPP_PPTPLayer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet)` with `payloadLen == 3`, even though `sizeof(ppp_pptp_header) == 4`. Inside the new layer, `PPP_PPTPLayer::parseNextLayer()` hits `if (m_DataLen <= headerLen) return;` with `m_DataLen == 3` and `headerLen == 4`, so it leaves `m_NextLayer == nullptr`. Later `Packet::computeCalculateFields()` reaches `PPP_PPTPLayer::computeCalculateFields()`, takes the `m_NextLayer == nullptr` arm, and writes `header->protocol = 0;` into bytes 2..3 of that 4-byte header. Because only three bytes back the layer, the second byte of that 2-byte store crosses the 31-byte heap allocation from `PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()`, matching the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` / `WRITE of size 2` in `pcpp::PPP_PPTPLayer::computeCalculateFields()`. The fix corroborates the missing obligation by adding `PPP_PPTPLayer::isDataValid(data, dataLen)` and changing the PPP branch in `GreLayer::parseNextLayer()` to fall back to `PayloadLayer` when `dataLen < sizeof(ppp_pptp_header)`.

source.description: Source. `GreLayer::parseNextLayer()` first materializes the vulnerability-relevant PPP payload extent from the attacker-controlled GRE flags and packet length.
source.value_from: `gt_results/arvo_42530184/poc` contains exactly 31 trailing packet-data bytes after its savefile record header, and the saved ASan allocation proves `PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()` later materialized a 31-byte raw packet before the crash. Those 31 bytes have a 20-byte IPv4 header followed by GRE bytes `20 20 88 0b 20 20 20 20`. On this tree, `getHeaderLen()` interprets GRE flags byte `0x20` as `keyBit == 1`, so `headerLen == 8`; with 11 bytes total in the GRE layer, this statement computes `payloadLen == 3` and `payload` points to the trailing bytes `20 20 20`.
source.note: This is the first project parser statement on the crashing path that turns the saved witness packet tail into the short PPP slice later cast to `ppp_pptp_header`.

root_cause.code: m_NextLayer = new PPP_PPTPLayer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet);
root_cause.description: Root cause. The PPP branch constructs `PPP_PPTPLayer` from a 3-byte payload without validating that `payloadLen` covers the 4-byte `ppp_pptp_header`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact site to `PPP_PPTPLayer::isDataValid(payload, payloadLen) ? static_cast<Layer*>(new PPP_PPTPLayer(...)) : static_cast<Layer*>(new PayloadLayer(...))`, and defines `isDataValid()` as `data && dataLen >= sizeof(ppp_pptp_header)`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The `m_NextLayer == nullptr` arm zeros the 2-byte PPP protocol field even though the layer has only 3 backing bytes.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow` / `WRITE of size 2` in `pcpp::PPP_PPTPLayer::computeCalculateFields()` and says the first invalid byte is 0 bytes to the right of the 31-byte heap region allocated by `pcpp::PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()`. On the witnessed `payloadLen == 3` path, this line is the only reachable 2-byte store in that function.

parser_admitted.code: m_NextLayer = new GREv0Layer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet);
parser_admitted.description: The staged packet reaches the vulnerable GRE parser path because the IPv4 protocol byte is 47 and `GreLayer::getGREVersion(payload, payloadLen)` classifies the payload as GREv0 instead of generic payload.
parser_admitted.condition: Static decoding of the staged witness shows raw byte 9 is `0x2f` (`PACKETPP_IPPROTO_GRE`) and the GRE bytes begin `20 20 88 0b ...`; the saved run also prints `IPv4 Layer`, `GRE Layer, version 0`, and `PPP for PPTP Layer` before the crash. Together that grounds this `GREv0Layer` admission before the later PPP dispatch.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant tainted scalar is the GRE payload length. This statement computes the would-be PPP payload size as 3 bytes.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The witnessed 31-byte packet buffer leaves 11 bytes after the 20-byte IPv4 header. Because GRE flags byte `0x20` sets `keyBit`, `getHeaderLen()` returns 8, and this subtraction materializes `payloadLen == 3`.
tainted_value_origin.note: That 3-byte extent is reused at the missing validation site in step 3 and explains why the later PPP parser immediately returns on `m_DataLen <= headerLen`.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01 reproduced only the vulnerable build. This Stage 02 trace uses the exact `patch.diff` to ground the missing validation obligation, but it did not execute a fixed build, so the remediation claim is source-grounded rather than runtime-confirmed.

The staged savefile packet-record header bytes do not themselves decode to `incl_len == 31`; they decode to `ts_sec=0x20202020`, `ts_usec=0x20202020`, `incl_len=0x20202020`, and `orig_len=31`. This trace therefore grounds the 31-byte packet extent only via the saved run (`PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()` allocation, the printed IPv4/GRE/PPP layer chain, and the file's trailing 31 packet bytes), not via a reconstructed libpcap malformed-record recovery rule.

The saved ASan frame for `pcpp::PPP_PPTPLayer::computeCalculateFields()` does not include a source line. Line 615 is derived source-groundedly because step 4 proves `m_NextLayer` remains null on the witnessed 3-byte PPP layer, leaving `header->protocol = 0;` as the only reachable 2-byte store in that function.

coarse_trace.summary: The 31-byte packet buffer witnessed in the saved run is admitted as IPv4/GREv0, and `GreLayer::parseNextLayer()` uses the GRE `keyBit` to derive an 8-byte GRE header and a 3-byte PPP payload.
The GRE protocol field `0x880b` selects the PPP branch, and vulnerable code still constructs `PPP_PPTPLayer` from `payloadLen == 3` with no `sizeof(ppp_pptp_header)` check.
The new PPP layer immediately hits `m_DataLen <= headerLen` (`3 <= 4`) and returns without parsing a next layer, leaving `m_NextLayer == nullptr`.
When packet field recomputation reaches the truncated PPP layer, the null-next-layer arm writes the 2-byte `protocol` field into a 3-byte buffer and ASan reports the saved heap-buffer-overflow write.

fine_trace.note: Source. `getHeaderLen()` reads GRE flags byte `0x20`, sees `keyBit == 1`, and returns 8. Because the packet buffer reaching GRE parsing is 31 bytes and the IPv4 header consumes 20, this step materializes a 3-byte GRE payload slice `20 20 20` for the next protocol.
The GRE protocol field is `0x880b`, so control enters the PPP branch rather than any of the IPv4/IPv6/VLAN/MPLS/Payload alternatives.

fine_trace.code: m_NextLayer = new PPP_PPTPLayer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The PPP branch instantiates `PPP_PPTPLayer` with `payloadLen == 3` even though `sizeof(ppp_pptp_header) == 4`. Vulnerable code performs no length check here; the fix inserts `PPP_PPTPLayer::isDataValid(payload, payloadLen)` at this exact statement.

When parsing the newly created PPP layer, `getHeaderLen()` returns 4 and the constructor-provided `m_DataLen` is still 3, so this guard returns immediately. The truncated layer stays in the packet and `m_NextLayer` remains null.

Sink. `Packet::computeCalculateFields()` later visits this truncated PPP layer. Because step 4 returned early and left `m_NextLayer == nullptr`, `computeCalculateFields()` takes its else-arm and writes two bytes at the `protocol` field offset. Only three bytes back the layer, so the second byte crosses the 31-byte raw packet allocation from `PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()`, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow write of size 2.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the first invalid byte is 0 bytes to the right of the 31-byte heap region allocated here.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan trace names `pcpp::PPP_PPTPLayer::computeCalculateFields()` in `Packet++/src/GreLayer.cpp`, and fine-trace step 5 is the only reachable 2-byte write in that function on the witnessed `m_NextLayer == nullptr` path.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The fine trace follows the same path established by the staged artifacts: the 31-byte packet buffer allocated by `PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()` is admitted through IPv4/GRE parsing, truncated into a 3-byte PPP layer at `GreLayer::parseNextLayer()`, and later written in `pcpp::PPP_PPTPLayer::computeCalculateFields()` with `pcpp::Packet::computeCalculateFields()` immediately above it in the saved stack.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Step 1's derived `payloadLen == 3` is reused by step 3 to construct the undersized PPP layer, causes step 4's `m_DataLen <= headerLen` early return, and thereby makes step 5 write the 2-byte `protocol` field past the 31-byte heap buffer.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 saved `docker exec gt-arvo_42530184-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` / `WRITE of size 2` in `pcpp::PPP_PPTPLayer::computeCalculateFields()` with caller `pcpp::Packet::computeCalculateFields()`.

format.name: pcap / raw IPv4 GREv0 packet with PPP ethertype
format.contract: Exactly the staged `gt_results/arvo_42530184/poc` file (71 bytes, sha256 `6c6d89edf944e9e513c5d5780b23d25c5cd591e01f6726e2b48a963f55a63c4a`). The reviewed artifacts prove that its saved vulnerable run materializes a 31-byte packet buffer whose bytes are `45 20 20 20 20 20 00 00 20 2f 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 88 0b 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`. Within that exact 31-byte witness, IPv4 byte 9 is `0x2f` (GRE) and GRE bytes `20 20 88 0b 20 20 20 20` make `keyBit == 1`, `GreLayer::getHeaderLen() == 8`, GRE protocol `0x880b`, and the remaining PPP payload exactly `20 20 20` (3 bytes). That exact 3-byte PPP tail is the trigger condition: vulnerable `GreLayer::parseNextLayer()` still constructs `PPP_PPTPLayer` from it, and `computeCalculateFields()` later overruns the 4-byte PPP header's `protocol` field.
